review_notes: I read the whole file and checked it for simp-interface problems. It declares no @[simp] lemmas, simp sets or simp-normal-form conventions. Every declaration is private or scoped, except the final `solution` theorem. The only simp uses are local: `simp only [IsRelDegree, key]`, `simpa [mul_assoc]`, and two `simp [ratPrime, Rat.HeightOneSpectrum.primesEquiv, ...ofPrime_asIdeal]` calls that unfold the private `ratPrime`. Those two calls prove `ratPrime ... .asIdeal` equals a comap in one place and a map in the other. They state different equalities, and both are used once, so a shared simp lemma would not clearly help. I found no sign of a rewrite cycle, competing rules, unwanted expansion or a missing canonical lemma. A `@[simp]` lemma on these private one-use helpers would be speculative and could pollute downstream simp sets. I did not search the other source roots for competing simp lemmas, so I may have missed one.
